source.title: When Models Refuse: Political Steerability and Feature Richness as Measures of Ideological Depth
source.authors: Shariar Kabir; Kevin M. Esterling; Yue Dong

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure data and the confusion matrices are flattened in the extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends SAE-based feature analysis to political representations in LLMs and reports results on recovered features and their ablation; it does not reproduce the original toy-network geometry experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition as motivation but does not test overlapping or nearly orthogonal directions, capacity competition, feature sparsity-dependent geometric transitions, or one-dimensional feature geometry. Prompt and activation-steering results are not included as rows because they do not by themselves measure whether SAE features are present or recoverable. Layer sweeps are used to select layers, not treated as results on the claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses public SAEs (GemmaScope, LlamaScope) as a tool to measure 'ideological depth' and compare political feature richness between Gemma-2-9b-it and Llama-3.1-8b-it. It cites superposition only as motivation. It does not test whether features are superposed, whether SAEs recover sparse features beyond some baseline, or any property of SAE features as units. Its feature counts, LLM-judged coherence and ablation-induced refusals measure differences between models in political competence, read through an SAE, not the claim. Differences between the two SAEs (separate training, base vs instruct for LlamaScope) are confounds the authors acknowledge.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. One correction: the headline '∼7.3× more political features' is the average number of active latents per statement. The total distinct-feature ratio (18458 vs 4412) is about 4.2×, yet the discussion states Gemma 'possesses ∼7.3× more political features'. The authors attribute Llama's refusals on benign political prompts to a capability deficit rather than to safety rules.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained LLMs, publicly available SAEs, feature description evaluations, and feature ablation; it does not use the original toy-network setup or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SAE feature counts depend on model and selected layer (14 for Llama, 20 for Gemma). The study also reports that responses vary by prompt and argumentative condition, but does not give a comparable condition sweep for the SAE feature-count result.

fits_no_version.finding: With same-size (131K) public SAEs, Gemma-2-9b-it activates 18458 distinct latents on 126 political statements, versus 4412 for Llama-3.1-8b-it. Ablating 71 selected Gemma latents raises its refusals.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The number and coherence of SAE latents active on a domain can index a model's domain competence, with low counts going with refusals.

record.problems: Only two similarly sized models are studied. The SAEs were trained on different corpora, which the authors acknowledge could confound comparisons. Feature coherence and predictive validity rely on GPT-4o-mini evaluation. Some figure results have no exact values in the text, and the authors note ablation may remove capability beyond political features.
record.rows_left_out: Steering and prompt-engineering outcomes were left out because they do not directly measure the versions concerning SAE-recoverable features or feature geometry. Output-score summary statistics from Table 2 were left out because they quantify selected-feature steering scores rather than whether the claimed representation is present or recoverable.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry, sparsity transition or near-orthogonality.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions.
No test of non-capacity origins of polysemanticity.
Uses SAEs as given. It does not test neuron-level distribution of features or SAE recovery against any baseline.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and V4 'supports' labels are overturned. The paper applies SAEs as an instrument and never questions or tests superposition or SAE recovery. The feature counts are compared across two different SAEs trained on different corpora, and LlamaScope is a base-model SAE. The steering and Table 2 output-score results are correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, overlap geometry, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether features compete for limited representational capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Tests political features extracted with SAEs in two LLMs, but not whether features are spread across many neurons or how the result generalizes beyond these models and political prompts.
Evaluates feature coherence and classification utility but does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the models.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Counted distinct SAE features activating for evaluation statements, excluding features activated for the BOS token.
rows.note: The paper reports this count among 131K possible SAE features.
rows.check: This is a count of SAE latents active on 126 political statements, with no baseline or control. It measures political feature richness via an SAE tool, not whether LLMs contain SAE-recoverable sparse features in the claim's sense.

rows.subject: llama-3.1-8b-it
rows.operation_detail: Counted distinct SAE features activating for evaluation statements, excluding features activated for the BOS token.
rows.note: The paper reports this count among 131K possible SAE features.
rows.check: Same as r1. The Llama count also comes from a base-model SAE applied to the instruct model, so the cross-model comparison is confounded.

rows.subject: llama-3.1-8b-it
rows.operation_detail: Counted SAE features with positive normalized mean amplitude difference.
rows.note: The paper reports the feature count directly.
rows.check: This is a count used to select features for STA-style steering (Δa>0). It is a selection quantity, not a result on the claim.

rows.subject: llama-3.1-8b-it
rows.operation_detail: Counted SAE features with positive normalized mean frequency difference.
rows.note: The paper reports the feature count directly.
rows.check: This is a selection quantity (Δf>0) for steering-feature selection, not a result on the claim.

rows.subject: gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Counted SAE features with positive normalized mean frequency difference.
rows.note: The paper lists the Δf count first for Gemma.
rows.check: This is a selection quantity. The paper's sentence order is ambiguous on whether 368 refers to Δf or Δa.

rows.subject: gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Counted SAE features with positive normalized mean amplitude difference.
rows.note: The paper lists the Δa count second for Gemma.
rows.check: This is a selection quantity (Δa>0), not a result on the claim.

rows.subject: gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Selected features with Δf > 0 or Δa > 0 for evaluation of steering effectiveness.
rows.note: Selection was based on positive frequency or amplitude difference.
rows.check: This is the number of features selected for output-score evaluation and ablation. It is a selection value and should not be a result row.

rows.subject: llama-3.1-8b-it
rows.operation_detail: Selected features with Δf > 0 or Δa > 0 for evaluation of steering effectiveness.
rows.note: Selection was based on positive frequency or amplitude difference.
rows.check: This is a selection value (16 features chosen) and should not be a result row.

rows.subject: gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated whether activated SAE feature descriptions supported classification of political statements.

conditions.value: classify statements into 12 political categories using feature descriptions

rows.note: A confidence score of 5 often indicated a confident failure to assign a category; the paper says this occurred less often for Gemma than for Llama.
rows.check: This is a GPT-4o-mini classification of political topic from Neuronpedia feature descriptions. It measures how much political signal the features carry, not whether the model represents features in superposition or whether SAEs recover them. The state 'partial' has no version to be partial against.

rows.subject: llama-3.1-8b-it
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated whether activated SAE feature descriptions supported classification of political statements.

conditions.value: classify statements into 12 political categories using feature descriptions

rows.note: A confidence score of 5 often indicated a confident failure to assign a category.
rows.check: Same as r9. The 69% confident-failure rate is read by the authors as a model capability deficit, not as SAE recovery failure.

rows.subject: gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Had GPT-4o-mini rate thematic coherence of activated feature sets.
rows.measure: Thematic coherence of SAE feature sets
rows.value: Higher on average than Llama; wider distribution, with additional concentration between 3.0 and 5.0
rows.note: No exact mean is stated in the text.
rows.check: This is an LLM-judged coherence rating of sets of activated features, a property of political-topic coverage. It does not bear on any version.

rows.subject: llama-3.1-8b-it
rows.operation_detail: Had GPT-4o-mini rate thematic coherence of activated feature sets.
rows.measure: Thematic coherence of SAE feature sets
rows.value: Scores tightly clustered around a median of 2
rows.note: The authors describe the feature sets as frequently mixing unrelated concepts.
rows.check: Same as r11. It is an LLM-judge coherence rating of feature sets, with no link to superposition or to SAE recovery.

rows.subject: gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated the 71 most salient political SAE features and measured null response rates.
rows.baseline: Original model had a negligible refusal rate
rows.value: Sharp increase in refusal rate across most topics; exact values are figure only
rows.note: The paper states the increase was sharp and says ablation sometimes removed capability, which could also contribute to failures.
rows.check: This measures the refusal rate after zero-ablating 71 selected SAE latents, which is a behavioural effect of the study's intervention. It says nothing about whether features are superposed or recoverable. The authors also note ablation may remove general capability.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE extraction from the two tested models at the selected layers
reader_labels.reason: The study extracts thousands of distinct activated political SAE features from each model and reports that ablation of Gemma's selected features increases refusals (r1, r2, r13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Comparative feature quality and predictive utility in Llama-3.1-8b-it versus Gemma-2-9b-it
reader_labels.reason: The reported feature counts and evaluations differ substantially: Llama has fewer activated features, more confident classification failures, and low coherence scores, while Gemma's feature descriptions perform better (r1, r2, r9, r10, r11, r12).
